text: Moving from NRZ (2 levels) to PAM-4 (4 levels) doubles the bits per symbol. What is the cost?
choices: Roughly 9.5 dB more SNR required for the same error rate, because the levels are a third as far apart
explanation: Four levels in the same voltage range means one third the spacing between adjacent levels, requiring substantially better SNR. Modern high-speed copper accepts this because bandwidth is the binding constraint and SNR is recoverable through equalisation and forward error correction.
